experiments.question: Does a walk-forward trigger x quantile grid find a configuration where the MA-compression pool beats its matched random control?
experiments.result: No configuration separated the pool from its control; pool-minus-control stayed inside -3.9bp..+4.8bp after the control function was corrected. Model metrics were bit-identical before and after that correction.

experiments.question: Was iteration_v1's anchored val rho=+0.465 (p=0.01, n=31) a real signal or a single-split regime coincidence?
experiments.result: not_reproducible. Under a 4-fold anchored walk-forward the same events give rho +0.219 on the corresponding fold and -0.151 on the next; weighted mean rho +0.065 over OOS n=140, inside a +-0.17 noise band. The original +0.465 was that split serving as both early-stopping selector and a single favourable regime. Secondary observation, recorded but not promoted to a conclusion: the anchored arm beat legacy in all 4 folds (paired sign test p~=0.06), so semantic anchoring helps direction-wise but not enough to matter. Pool level unchanged: anchored all-minus-control -5.4bp, legacy +4.8bp -- both indistinguishable from same-month same-volatility-bucket random entry.
experiments.single_variable: decision anchor (legacy zone_start vs anchored causal trigger)

experiments.question: Does a strict platform definition v2, adjudicated by the owner rather than by a threshold, isolate a subset of compression events that the loose pool dilutes?
experiments.result: definition_and_review_gallery_only. P04 produced the definition and a decision_view/outcome_view review gallery; no model was trained and no economic claim was made or tested. Carried forward as an open question, not as evidence.
experiments.single_variable: platform definition (loose scanner vs strict v2)

experiments.question: Without YOLO, using only OHLCV, SMA/EMA 20/60/120, ATR and 27 causal semantic features, can a LightGBM regressor rank MA-compression candidates so that the top of the ranking more often precedes a profitable SHORT?
experiments.result: underperformed_matched_random_control. Validation spearman +0.167 (p=0.28) did not survive into test, where it reversed to -0.068 (p=0.68). The decisive line is the matched control (same symbol, same month, same ATR tercile, same horizon, same cost): control +19.9bp gross on validation against -14.6bp for the whole candidate pool, i.e. the compression pool was 34.5bp WORSE than random short entries; on test, -2.0bp against -39.1bp, worse by 37.1bp. The val top-decile +62.6bp sits on 5 samples during a falling-ETH window and is short beta, not model skill. On test the naive "tighter is better" dispersion baseline (+0.349, p=0.027) outranked the 27-feature model.
experiments.single_variable: ranking model vs single-feature dispersion baseline
